title: LaST-VLA: Thinking in Latent Spatio-Temporal Space for Vision-Language-Action in Autonomous Driving
claim: Existing paradigms each sacrifice efficiency, grounding, stability or interpretability; ours adds supervision to a latent reasoning step and satisfies all four.
layout: 4 stacked panels, left-to-right flow, checkmark/cross scorecards at right
description: Four horizontal rows, separated by dashed lines, compare VLA paradigms. Each row has Image and Text inputs with arrows into a gray VLM box. The VLM outputs to a dotted box showing a car icon and a trajectory. A rounded scorecard on the right lists Inference Efficiency, Physical Grounding, Reasoning Stability and Interpretability, each marked with a green check or red cross. (a) Direct VLA has no reasoning module. (b) Explicit textual CoT adds a green 'Discrete Textual CoT' box above the VLM. (c) Naive latent CoT sits in a blue dashed region with a red warning icon and mostly red crosses. (d) Ours, in bold, adds a yellow 'Latent CoT' block fed by a blue '3D / WM Supervision' box, with a green check badge and all four checks. The eye goes to the final row and the contrast in check marks.
caption: Comparison of VLA Paradigms. (a) Direct VLA is efficient but lacks reasoning. (b) Explicit Textual CoT is interpretable but suffers high latency and hallucinations. (c) Naive Latent CoT (w/o supervision) is efficient but unstable (model collapse). (d) Our Spatio-Temporal Latent CoT (supervision) aligns latent features with physical priors, achieving efficiency, stability, and grounding.
abstract: While Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have revolutionized autonomous driving by unifying perception and planning, their reliance on explicit textual Chain-of-Thought (CoT) leads to semantic-perceptual decoupling and perceptual-symbolic conflicts. Recent shifts toward latent reasoning attempt to bypass these bottlenecks by thinking in continuous hidden space. However, without explicit intermediate constraints, standard latent CoT often operates as a physics-agnostic representation. To address this, we propose the Latent Spatio-Temporal VLA (LaST-VLA), a framework shifting the reasoning paradigm from discrete symbolic processing into a physically grounded Latent Spatio-Temporal CoT. By implementing a dual-feature alignment mechanism, we distill geometric constraints from 3D foundation models and dynamic foresight from world models directly into the latent space. Coupled with a progressive SFT training strategy that transitions from feature alignment to trajectory generation, and refined via Reinforcement Learning with Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) to ensure safety and rule compliance. \method~setting a new record on NAVSIM v1 (91.3 PDMS) and NAVSIM v2 (87.1 EPDMS), while excelling in spatial-temporal reasoning on SURDS and NuDynamics benchmarks.
